# ledger_commitment (Resource)

A recurring commitment definition: what is owed, how much, in which currency and on which schedule. It is user data, kept apart from bank facts. The dated occurrences and their payment state (paid, upcoming, overdue) are derived by Ledger from it and from bank transactions and manual records, and are never managed here.

**Amounts are exact decimal strings** (`"850.00"`), never numbers, and keep the scale written. Amounts of different currencies are never combined or converted.

**Changing terms** (amount, currency, schedule, start or end date) reaches Ledger's unpaid occurrences from today in the reporting time zone: overdue unpaid occurrences keep their old terms, and paid history never changes. The API's `effective_from` is not exposed; set a future-dated change through the API if you need one.

**Destroy** deletes the definition and its unpaid occurrences. Ledger refuses while an occurrence has live payment evidence (a manual payment or a confirmed bank match); set `end_date` to stop such a commitment instead. A destroyed commitment that still has history is archived by Ledger and no longer appears in any read.

Import with the identifier: `terraform import ledger_commitment.example <id>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Amounts are exact decimal strings with a currency, never numbers.
resource "ledger_commitment" "rent" {
  name            = "Rent"
  kind            = "service"
  amount          = "850.00"
  currency        = "EUR"
  start_date      = "2026-01-01"
  priority        = "essential"
  match_tolerance = "0.50" # a booked payment up to 0.50 EUR short may still be confirmed automatically

  schedule = {
    frequency = "monthly"
    interval  = 1 # every month; 3 = quarterly
    day       = 1
  }

  # What you know about the creditor's grace. Omit the block to record nothing.
  leeway = {
    kind       = "period"
    days       = 5
    conditions = "after written notice"
    source     = "lease clause 7"
  }
}

# A quarterly commitment that ends. A day past the end of a month falls on that month's last day.
resource "ledger_commitment" "vps" {
  name       = "VPS"
  kind       = "server"
  amount     = "30.00"
  currency   = "USD"
  start_date = "2026-01-31"
  end_date   = "2027-12-31"

  schedule = {
    frequency = "monthly"
    interval  = 3
    day       = 31
  }
}

# An annual commitment. February 29 falls on February 28 in years that are not leap years.
resource "ledger_commitment" "domain" {
  name       = "example.org"
  kind       = "domain"
  amount     = "12.50"
  currency   = "EUR"
  start_date = "2024-02-29"
  priority   = "flexible"

  schedule = {
    frequency = "annual"
    month     = 2
    day       = 29
  }

  leeway = {
    kind  = "deadline"
    until = "2026-12-31"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `amount` (String) The amount due at each occurrence, an exact decimal greater than zero written as a string, for example `"850.00"`. Its scale is kept. Never write it as a number.
- `currency` (String) The ISO 4217 currency code of `amount` and `match_tolerance`, three upper-case letters.
- `kind` (String) What the commitment pays for: `service`, `server` (servers and VPSs), `domain`, `subscription` or `debt_repayment`.
- `name` (String) The name, 1 to 100 characters.
- `schedule` (Attributes) When it falls due. A day past the end of a month falls on that month's last day, and an annual February 29 falls on February 28 in years that are not leap years. A monthly schedule counts its interval from the month of `start_date`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--schedule))
- `start_date` (String) The first day the commitment applies, `YYYY-MM-DD`, not before 1900-01-01.

### Optional

- `end_date` (String) The last day the commitment applies (inclusive), `YYYY-MM-DD`, not before `start_date`. Omit for open-ended.
- `leeway` (Attributes) What you know about the grace the creditor allows after a due date. Entered by you only: never inferred from payment history, bank data or a model, with no default length. It only annotates an overdue occurrence; it never moves a due date or hides an obligation. Omitting the block records nothing, which is not the same as `kind = "unknown"` (you do not know) or `kind = "none"` (you state there is no grace). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--leeway))
- `match_tolerance` (String) How far a booked bank payment may fall short of `amount`, in `currency`, and still be confirmed automatically by Ledger's matching (an exact decimal string of zero or more). Omit for none: only the exact amount then confirms automatically. A payment above `amount` is never confirmed automatically.
- `notes` (String) Free-text notes, 1 to 2000 characters. Do not put secrets or account numbers here.
- `priority` (String) How important paying on time is: `essential`, `important` or `flexible`. Omit when not prioritised.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When it was created (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `id` (String) The Ledger identifier (a ULID). It never changes.
- `updated_at` (String) When it last changed (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `version` (Number) The optimistic-concurrency version (the ETag). Changes are sent against the version Terraform last read; a stale one fails instead of overwriting.

<a id="nestedatt--schedule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `schedule`

Required:

- `day` (Number) The day of the month, 1 to 31. For an annual schedule it must exist in that month in a leap year.
- `frequency` (String) `monthly` or `annual`.

Optional:

- `interval` (Number) Monthly only, required there: months between due dates, 1 to 120 (1 = every month, 3 = quarterly).
- `month` (Number) Annual only, required there: the month, 1 to 12.


<a id="nestedatt--leeway"></a>
### Nested Schema for `leeway`

Required:

- `kind` (String) `unknown`, `none`, `period` (days after each due date) or `deadline` (a fixed date).

Optional:

- `conditions` (String) What the grace depends on, as you know it (1 to 500 characters).
- `consequences` (String) Fees or other consequences of paying late that you know of (1 to 500 characters). Free text; it is not counted in any total.
- `days` (Number) Required for `period` (1 to 365), not allowed otherwise.
- `source` (String) Where the information comes from, such as a contract clause or a letter (1 to 200 characters).
- `until` (String) Required for `deadline` (`YYYY-MM-DD`): occurrences due on or before it are covered. Not allowed otherwise.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by the commitment's Ledger identifier.
terraform import ledger_commitment.rent 01JD3Y4C8V9M2Q7W5R6T0XZBNA
```
